A short list of the resources most useful for this course. Please let
me know if there are other links that you think should be included on
this page!

[Weekly "Stats Chats"](https://guides.library.unr.edu/StatsChats) at
the UNR library: drop-in help with statistics and R.

# The textbook

- [Ecological Models and Data in R](https://math.mcmaster.ca/~bolker/emdbook/)
  (Bolker): book page, with R code, data, and errata. The `emdbook` R
  package has the data sets.

# Math and probability background

Short, visual introductions to the math this course uses. Good places to
start if a topic feels shaky.

- [Essence of Calculus](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/calculus)
  (3Blue1Brown): derivatives, integrals, and the fundamental theorem,
  with almost no algebra.
- [Essence of Linear Algebra](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/linear-algebra)
  (3Blue1Brown): vectors, matrix multiplication, determinants, inverses,
  and eigenvalues as geometry.
- [Probability](https://www.3blue1brown.com/topics/probability)
  (3Blue1Brown): includes
  [Bayes' theorem](https://www.3blue1brown.com/lessons/bayes-theorem),
  the [central limit theorem](https://www.3blue1brown.com/lessons/clt),
  and why the normal distribution has a $\pi$ in it
  ([the Gaussian integral](https://www.3blue1brown.com/lessons/gaussian-integral)).
- [Seeing Theory](https://seeing-theory.brown.edu/): interactive
  introduction to probability, distributions, inference, and regression.
- [The Distribution Explorer](https://distribution-explorer.github.io/):
  the common distributions, what stories generate them, and how they
  relate, with interactive plots.

# Mathematical statistics

- [The geometry of statistics](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLmtbsGjqSdcbF261LACoVqibOFCGQT3GI)
  (Sam Levey): how linear algebra explains regression, variance, and
  more; a good follow-up to the linear algebra videos.
- [STAT 414: Introduction to Probability Theory](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat414/)
  and [STAT 415: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics](https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat415/)
  (Penn State): free course notes covering random variables,
  expectation, distributions, likelihood, and maximum likelihood
  estimation, with worked examples.
- [Statistical Rethinking](https://xcelab.net/rm/) (McElreath): book and
  free [lecture videos](https://www.youtube.com/@rmcelreath). A
  readable, ecology-friendly path through likelihood, Bayesian
  inference, multilevel models, and causal reasoning.

# R and RStudio

- [Download R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and
  [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
- [RStudio projects](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/200526207-Using-RStudio-Projects):
  keep each analysis in its own folder.
- [R Bootcamp](https://kevintshoemaker.github.io/R-Bootcamp/): my
  introductory R workshop.
- [Hands-On Programming with R](https://rstudio-education.github.io/hopr/)
  (Grolemund): writing your own functions, loops, and simulations.
- [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) (Wickham et al.): data
  wrangling and plotting with the tidyverse.
- [Coding Club](https://ourcodingclub.github.io/): short R tutorials
  for ecologists and environmental scientists.
- [Posit cheatsheets](https://posit.co/resources/cheatsheets/): one- or
  two-page references for R Markdown, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, and more.
- [R Markdown: The Definitive Guide](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/)
  (Xie et al.): reports, slides, and websites (this site is built with
  R Markdown).
- [Happy Git and GitHub for the useR](https://happygitwithr.com/)
  (Bryan): version control with Git and GitHub from RStudio.

# Bayesian inference, MCMC, and Stan

- [Bayes Rules!](https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/) (Johnson, Ott, and
  Dogucu): a free introductory Bayesian textbook with R code.
- [Interactive gallery of MCMC samplers](https://chi-feng.github.io/mcmc-demo/app.html)
  (Chi Feng): watch Metropolis, Gibbs, HMC, and NUTS explore different
  posteriors.
- [MCMC sampling for dummies](https://twiecki.github.io/blog/2015/11/10/mcmc-sampling/)
  (Wiecki): a Metropolis sampler built from scratch.
- [A conceptual introduction to Hamiltonian Monte Carlo](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.02434)
  (Betancourt): why HMC works, with very little math.
- [Stan](https://mc-stan.org/): the
  [documentation](https://mc-stan.org/docs/) (user's guide, functions
  reference) and the
  [getting started with cmdstanr](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/articles/cmdstanr.html)
  vignette.
- [brms](https://paul-buerkner.github.io/brms/): fit Stan models with
  `lme4`-style formulas.
- [Bayesian workflow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.01808) (Gelman et
  al.): building, checking, and comparing models in practice.
- [NIMBLE](https://r-nimble.org/) and
  [JAGS](https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io/): BUGS-language samplers,
  useful for models with discrete latent variables.

# Model comparison and performance

- [A practical guide to selecting models for exploration, inference, and prediction in ecology](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.3336)
  (Tredennick et al. 2021, *Ecology*).
- [Cross-validation FAQ](https://users.aalto.fi/~ave/CV-FAQ.html)
  (Vehtari): what cross-validation and LOO estimate, and when to trust
  them. See also the [loo package](https://mc-stan.org/loo/) vignettes.
- [An Introduction to Statistical Learning](https://www.statlearning.com/)
  (James et al.): free book; its chapters on cross-validation and on
  ridge and lasso regression are especially clear.
- [DHARMa](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/DHARMa/vignettes/DHARMa.html):
  simulation-based residual checks for GLMs and mixed models.

# Causal inference

- [DAGitty](https://www.dagitty.net/): draw a causal diagram and find
  which variables to adjust for.
- [The Effect](https://theeffectbook.net/) (Huntington-Klein): a free,
  readable book on causal diagrams and research design.

# Mixed models

- [GLMM FAQ](https://bbolker.github.io/mixedmodels-misc/glmmFAQ.html)
  (Bolker): the standard reference for practical questions about
  fitting mixed models in R (convergence warnings, singular fits,
  choosing a package, testing random effects).
- [A brief introduction to mixed effects modelling and multi-model inference in ecology](https://peerj.com/articles/4794/)
  (Harrison et al. 2018, *PeerJ*).
- [Fitting linear mixed-effects models using lme4](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v067i01)
  (Bates et al. 2015): how `lme4` works, including the formula syntax.
- [glmmTMB vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glmmTMB/vignettes/glmmTMB.pdf):
  zero-inflated and dispersion models.

# Smooths and GAMs

- [GAMs in R](https://noamross.github.io/gams-in-r-course/) (Ross): a
  free interactive course using `mgcv`.
- [Hierarchical generalized additive models in ecology](https://peerj.com/articles/6876/)
  (Pedersen et al. 2019, *PeerJ*).

# Time series and spatial data

- [Applied time series analysis for fisheries and environmental sciences](https://atsa-es.github.io/atsa-labs/)
  (Holmes, Scheuerell, and Ward): labs on ARMA and state-space models.
- [Forecasting: Principles and Practice](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)
  (Hyndman and Athanasopoulos): autocorrelation, ARIMA, and forecasting.
- [Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/) (Lovelace et al.):
  spatial data in R with `sf` and `terra`.

# Data sources {#Data_links}

Public data sets for final projects:

- [Dryad](https://datadryad.org/): data behind published papers.
- [EDI Data Portal](https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/home.jsp):
  LTER and other long-term ecological data.
- [DataONE](https://search.dataone.org/): searches many environmental
  data repositories at once.
- [NEON data portal](https://data.neonscience.org/): standardized
  ecological data from sites across the US.
- [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org/): species occurrence records worldwide.
